findings.description: All invocations of the wrapped function now share and clear a single statistics dict. Each call's `stats.clear()` wipes the dict that other in-flight calls are using, and they all write into the same dict.
findings.rationale: Trigger: the same decorated function runs concurrently (threads) or recursively or reentrantly. The first call's counters are cleared by the second call's `stats.clear()`, and both write `attempt_number` and `idle_for` into one dict. Impact: statistics are corrupted or reset mid-call. The previous code gave each call a fresh dict via the copy, which avoided this.

findings.description: The shared statistics dict is cleared on every call. Concurrent coroutines of the same async-wrapped function share one dict, so each new call resets the stats of the calls already running.
findings.rationale: Trigger: `asyncio.gather` of several calls to the same retry-decorated coroutine. Each call executes `stats.clear()` and then writes to the same dict. Impact: `attempt_number` and `idle_for` are overwritten or reset across calls, so the statistics are wrong.
